findings.position: Change confirmed with supplier: changes are confirmed, but sometimes using contact details taken from the request itself. Familiar caller still verified: a follow-up call from the 'supplier' is accepted as confirmation.
findings.mechanism: A fraudster, often impersonating the supplier by email, voice or video, has the bank account changed.
findings.whyItMatters: Changed supplier bank details are the most common route for payment fraud, and cloned voices now defeat call-backs that rely on recognition.
methodRisks: Payment redirection through false bank details or impersonation

findings.title: A supplier is set up with an account it does not own

findings.mechanism: Payments go to an employee's or fraudster's account from the first invoice.
findings.whyItMatters: Confirming account ownership at onboarding stops both fictitious and impersonated suppliers being paid into accounts they do not own; added after the review's isolated-weakness probe.
methodRisks: Payment redirection through false bank details or impersonation

risks.cause: customer logins protected is partly in place
risks.consequence: Customer accounts without takeover protection are drained with stolen passwords.
risks.currentPosition: Multi-factor authentication is offered, but customers can opt out.
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: A security compromise is not notified
risks.statement: The Regulator and affected people are not told, so they cannot protect themselves, because compromises reported as POPIA requires is partly in place.
risks.cause: compromises reported as POPIA requires is partly in place
risks.consequence: POPIA section 22 requires notification as soon as reasonably possible.
risks.currentPosition: A compromise would be handled as it happens, without a set process.
risks.treatment: C93 Compromises reported as POPIA requires; C94 Affected people warned
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: A help desk reset hands an attacker access
risks.statement: An impersonator persuades the help desk to reset a password or authenticator, because help desk resets verified is partly in place.
risks.cause: help desk resets verified is partly in place
risks.currentPosition: Most resets need verification through a trusted route, such as the person's manager or a number on file.
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: Systems that move money are accessed without strong sign-in
risks.statement: Remote access, cloud or banking systems rely on passwords alone, because multi-factor on critical systems is not in place.
risks.cause: multi-factor on critical systems is not in place
risks.currentPosition: These systems are protected by passwords only.
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: Personal information is over-exposed or kept too long
risks.statement: Too many people can reach or export personal information, or records outlive their purpose, because access to personal information limited is partly in place.
risks.cause: access to personal information limited is partly in place
risks.currentPosition: Access is limited for some systems only.
risks.treatment: C97 Access to personal information limited
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: A SIM swap defeats one-time PIN approvals
risks.statement: Approvals sent by SMS are intercepted, because approval numbers protected is partly in place.
risks.cause: approval numbers protected is partly in place
risks.currentPosition: Staff have been told about SIM swaps, but nothing has been changed.
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: An AI assistant is manipulated by hidden instructions
risks.statement: Instructions planted in emails or documents make an assistant leak data or act, because assistant permissions limited is partly in place.
risks.cause: assistant permissions limited is partly in place
risks.currentPosition: Assistant permissions limited: reported in place only in some areas, cases or periods.
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: The organisation's own information helps attackers
risks.statement: Published staff details and routines make impersonation easier, because staff guided on what not to share is not in place.
risks.cause: staff guided on what not to share is not in place
risks.currentPosition: Staff guided on what not to share: reported as not in place.
risks.treatment: C100 Staff guided on what not to share
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: A compromise is not contained quickly
risks.statement: Accounts stay compromised while suppliers and customers keep receiving instructions, because compromise playbook is not in place.
risks.cause: compromise playbook is not in place
risks.currentPosition: There is no plan; each case would be handled from scratch.
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: The organisation is impersonated to defraud others
risks.statement: Fake websites, accounts or job adverts in the organisation's name collect money or personal information, because brand impersonation monitored and removed is not in place.
risks.cause: brand impersonation monitored and removed is not in place
risks.currentPosition: Brand impersonation monitored and removed: reported as not in place.
risks.treatment: C102 Brand impersonation monitored and removed
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

risks.title: Spoofed email in the organisation's name deceives staff, suppliers or customers
risks.statement: Emails that appear to come from the organisation's own domain carry false payment instructions, because domain protected against spoofing is partly in place.
risks.cause: domain protected against spoofing is partly in place
risks.currentPosition: Domain protected against spoofing: partly in place.
risks.rating: Not rated. MK has not approved a method for rating likelihood, impact or priority.

schemeNames: Staff do not know or understand what is expected
controls.reported: Training on joining: reported in place only in some areas, cases or periods.
controls.standard: Training on joining: in place across everything it should cover.
controls.target: Every new employee completes fraud and ethics training in their first month, covering the code of conduct, how to report concerns and the schemes relevant to their role.
controls.archetype: Training that reaches everyone it should
controls.recordText: Training completion record: each new employee, the training completed and the date.
activities: Set the content and who must complete it, using current schemes relevant to their work.
Track completion monthly, and follow up anyone who has not completed it.
Refresh the content each year, and test understanding where the risk is highest.
controls.successMeasure: Every new employee completed the training within their first month, and completion is recorded.
controls.onFailure: Follow up incomplete training with the person's manager, and restrict access to sensitive duties where the risk requires it.
controls.questionText: Do all employees receive fraud and ethics training when they join?
controls.answerLabel: Partly: only in some areas, cases or periods

schemeNames: Donations or sponsorships channel bribes
controls.reported: Recipients checked for links: reported in place only in some areas, cases or periods.

controls.questionText: Are recipients checked for links to public officials, customers' decision-makers and employees before money is committed?
controls.answerLabel: Partly: only in some areas, cases or periods

controls.reported: Directors compared with staff: reported as not in place.
controls.standard: Directors compared with staff: in place across everything it should cover.

schemeNames: Supplier payments are diverted through changed bank details
controls.reported: Changes are confirmed, but sometimes using contact details taken from the request itself.
controls.standard: Every change is confirmed with the supplier using contact details already on file before it takes effect.
controls.improving: Confirmations are checked independently, and attempted fraudulent changes are tracked and shared with staff.
controls.records: Change records with call-back notes, the procedure, a sample of recent changes.
controls.target: Every change to a supplier's bank details is confirmed with the supplier, using contact details already on file and not those in the request, before it takes effect.
controls.archetype: Verify a change through a known channel
controls.recordText: Bank detail change log: each request, how and by whom it was confirmed, the number used and the date the change took effect.
activities: Write the confirmation step into the procedure: a call to the supplier on a number already on file, never details supplied with the request.
Limit who can make the change in the supplier master file, and log how each change was confirmed.
Check the changes to suppliers' bank details made in the last six months against the log, and confirm any that were not verified.
controls.successMeasure: Every change to a supplier's bank details made in the period was confirmed with the supplier on contact details already on file before it took effect, or is a recorded and approved exception.
controls.onFailure: Suspend any change to a supplier's bank details that was not confirmed until it is verified, and check whether any payment, delivery or access used it.
controls.questionText: Is every change to a supplier's bank details confirmed with the supplier using contact details already on file, not those in the change request?
controls.answerLabel: Changes are confirmed, but sometimes using contact details taken from the request itself.

schemeNames: Supplier payments are diverted through changed bank details
controls.reported: A follow-up call from the 'supplier' is accepted as confirmation.
controls.standard: The procedure requires a call back on the number on file regardless of any incoming call or video, and staff know why.
controls.improving: The rule is tested, for example with simulated calls, and staff report approaches of this kind.
controls.records: The procedure wording, training material on cloned voices, simulation or test results.
controls.target: A call back on the number on file is required for every change request, whatever an incoming call or video appears to show, and staff know why.
controls.archetype: An organisation-wide rule that people follow
controls.recordText: Verification rule record: the rule, briefing records and the results of each test.

Brief staff who process changes to supplier details, including executives and their assistants, and record who has been briefed.
Test the rule at least once a year, for example with a simulated request, and act on the result.

controls.questionText: If a change request is followed by a call or video call from someone who sounds or looks like the supplier's usual contact, is the change still confirmed by calling a number already on file?

decisions.decision: Name one accountable executive for each area with open or unresolved scenarios: ethics (1), procurement (13), people (11), customers (10), assets (9) and digital channels (14).

decisions.recommendedDirection: The method suggests: ethics lead for ethics, procurement lead for procurement, HR and payroll lead for people, commercial and customer lead for customers and operations lead for assets, and the leads named in the register for the rest.

decisions.decision: Decide the order in which the open scenarios are addressed, using explicit factors.
decisions.why: MK has not approved a method for rating fraud risks, so this report does not rank them, and neither its order nor the method's tiers is a ranking.
decisions.recommendedDirection: Settle conflicting answers and open questions first. Then weigh, for each scenario, how far its control is reported in place, whether money, pay, cash or stock can leave without it, how much activity passes through the process, whether another control would detect a loss, and how many other scenarios the same control serves. The finding register gives the facts the assessment holds for the first and last of these; management supplies the rest.
decisions.consequenceOfDelay: Effort is spread across every scenario at once, or follows the order of this report, which is not a ranking.

roadmap.title: Proposed stages for the first 90 days
roadmap.interpretation: These are proposed planning stages for starting the work, not deadlines, contractual dates or estimates. Each window shows when a stage could begin once what it depends on is known and decided. How long a control takes to design, put in place and show to be operating depends on the organisation, and management sets its own dates.

stages.stage: 30 days, proposed: establish the facts and owners
stages.primaryOutcome: Answers that conflict are settled, open questions and outstanding answers are answered, and each area with open scenarios has an accountable executive.

actions.action: Obtain the 7 outstanding answers from the functions named in the register.
actions.deliverable: An answer, or an open item with a named owner, for each question.
actions.completionTest: No question is left declined or unanswered without an owner.

actions.action: Name the accountable executive for each area, and decide the order of work using explicit factors.
actions.deliverable: Named executives and a recorded order of work, with the factors behind it.
actions.completionTest: Every open scenario is selected, deferred with a reason or accepted at the right level.

stages.stage: 60 days, proposed: approve designs and begin
stages.primaryOutcome: Approved designs exist for the controls management selected, and the first are being put in place.

actions.action: Approve the target design for each selected control, using the target practice, records and measure in the register, and begin putting the first designs in place.
actions.deliverable: Approved designs, each with an owner and the records it will keep.
actions.completionTest: Each selected control has an approved design and a named owner.

stages.stage: 90 days, proposed: start operating and report
stages.primaryOutcome: The first approved controls have started operating and the oversight body has the status of every open scenario. Whether a control works is known only after its first full cycle, which for many controls ends after 90 days.

actions.action: Start operating the approved designs, and begin each control's first full operating cycle.
actions.deliverable: A start date and an operating record for each control.
actions.completionTest: Each control has started operating; its success measure is checked when its first full cycle ends.

actions.action: Report the status of each open scenario to the board.
actions.deliverable: A one-page status per scenario: owner, controls in place, controls outstanding, next step.
actions.completionTest: The status is received and minuted.
